headline: ENTREE RESOURCES HOLES 125m @ 1.45% CuEq AT OYU TOLGOI JV — Hugo North Extension Results In As Copper Surges
snippet: Entrée Resources (TSX: ETG) reported additional Hugo North Extension drill results from its Oyu Tolgoi joint venture in Mongolia, with highlight hole UGD1025A returning 125.31 metres grading 1.45% copper equivalent. The result adds to the underground resource at one of the world's largest undeveloped copper-gold deposits, operated by Rio Tinto. The release comes alongside an update on outstanding mining licence matters that have dogged Entrée's ability to fully monetise its minority joint venture interest.

headline: COLLECTIVE MINING EXTENDS APOLLO HIGH-GRADE CORE TO 150.5m @ 1.46g/t AuEq — Five Rigs Drilling Ahead of 2027 Resource
snippet: Collective Mining (TSX: CNL) extended the high-grade core at its Apollo target in Colombia's Guayabales project, reporting 150.5 metres at 1.46 g/t gold equivalent from approximately 189 metres depth, including a 42-metre interval at 3.6 g/t gold equivalent. Five drill rigs are currently operating across the 40,000-metre 2026 program, with assays pending on a further 25 holes. The company is targeting a maiden mineral resource estimate in early 2027.

headline: SABLE RESOURCES' FIRST ZORRO COPPER DRILLING CONFIRMS MINERALIZATION — 200m Depths Tested in San Juan, Argentina
snippet: Sable Resources (TSXV: SAE) reported all assay results from its first diamond drilling program at the Zorro Project in San Juan Province, Argentina, confirming copper mineralization at Zorro North to depths of approximately 200 metres. Structural complexity at the Zorro Copper target limited continuity of mineralization, though the company identifies areas with continued exploration potential. San Juan hosts several operating copper mines and is the province where Challenger Gold's Hualilán project is also advancing.

headline: BAYHORSE SILVER DRILLS 886 METRES IN 6 UNDERGROUND HOLES — Oregon Mine's IP-Target Program Returns Results with One Hole Pending
snippet: Bayhorse Silver (TSXV: BHS) reported results from six of seven underground holes totaling 886 metres, targeting four induced-polarization anomalies identified in a 2025 IP survey at its Oregon silver mine. Drilling from underground access reduces costs relative to surface drilling and allows tighter targeting of the sub-surface anomalies. One final hole assay remains pending, with results expected shortly.

headline: ABU DHABI'S IRH BIDS $464M ALL-CASH FOR KENMARE'S MOZAMBIQUE ILMENITE MINE — Acquisition Requires Maputo Regulatory Sign-Off
snippet: Abu Dhabi-based International Resources Holding (IRH) has outlined the financial terms of a possible all-cash acquisition of Dublin-listed Kenmare Resources, valuing the company at approximately £352.8 million ($464 million USD) on a fully diluted basis. Kenmare operates the Moma Titanium Minerals Mine in Mozambique — one of the world's largest ilmenite operations, supplying titanium dioxide feedstock for pigment manufacturing globally. The deal requires approval from Mozambican authorities and other conditions; IRH's principal shareholders include Abu Dhabi holding company ADQ.

headline: GOLD MINERS RSI NEAR 10 — 'Rarely Seen' Oversold Extreme Hits ETFs Even as Metals Bounce
snippet: A November 27 Stockhouse analysis reports that relative strength indicators for gold mining ETFs have fallen close to 10 — a level rarely observed outside outright capitulation events. Despite Friday's rebound, the RSI remains at an extreme that historically precedes multi-week recoveries, suggesting momentum sellers may be nearing exhaustion. The piece frames the technical backdrop as one of the most compelling contrarian setups in years, even as macro headwinds from the Fed's rate-hike posture remain in place.

headline: CRASH INCOMING? BUY AGNICO EAGLE AND FRANCO-NEVADA FIRST — Motley Fool Makes the Case for Miners as Market Hedges
snippet: A November 26 Motley Fool piece argues retail investors bracing for a market downturn should own Agnico Eagle Mines and Franco-Nevada as defensive portfolio positions. Agnico is cited for its all-North-American production base, low geopolitical risk, and net cash balance sheet — rare at current gold prices. Franco-Nevada earns royalties rather than operating mines, insulating it from cost blowouts while maintaining full upside exposure to gold without the operational leverage that has punished producers in 2026.

headline: NOVEMBER EXPORT CONTROLS EXPOSED EVERY GAP IN WESTERN CRITICAL MINERAL SUPPLY — Skillings Maps the Vulnerabilities
snippet: Skillings Mining Review's analysis of November 2026's critical mineral export control escalation maps specific Western vulnerabilities: near-zero non-Chinese antimony refining capacity, minimal gallium and germanium alternatives, and deep reliance on Chinese processing for most strategic metals even where mining occurs elsewhere. The piece argues the gap between announced diversification plans and operational alternative supply has never been more visible — and that junior miners in key jurisdictions stand to benefit as policy shifts to incentives.

headline: CORPORATE JAPAN RACES TO REBUILD RARE EARTH SUPPLY CHAIN AMID CHINA CURBS — Honda, Shin-Etsu Among Companies Signing New Offtakes
snippet: Japanese manufacturers and trading houses are accelerating efforts to build a non-Chinese rare earth supply chain in response to Beijing's export control tightening in late 2026, according to Nikkei Asia. Companies from Honda to Shin-Etsu Chemical are expanding offtake agreements with producers in Australia, Canada, and Africa, revisiting dormant projects from the 2010s supply-chain scare. Japan's vulnerability is acute: the country relies heavily on rare earth permanent magnets for automotive, robotics, and defence applications, with limited domestic refining capacity.

headline: NON-CHINA RARE EARTH ROUTES: Which Ones Are ACTUALLY Producing Qualified Supply? — Yttrium Gap Is $1.1M vs $9,000
snippet: An analysis from Discovery Alert examines which non-Chinese rare earth supply routes are genuinely operational versus announced-but-not-producing, using the yttrium oxide price gap — roughly $1.15 million per tonne in Europe versus $9,144 in China — as evidence that qualified alternative supply remains severely limited. Heavy rare earth separation, metallization, and specialty alloy manufacturing are identified as the critical chokepoints where Western investment remains most insufficient, with a small number of junior developers positioned at those bottlenecks.

headline: WHY GOLD MINERS ALWAYS FALL HARDER THAN GOLD — And the Simple Checklist to Find the Ones That Recover First
snippet: A Discovery Alert analysis explains the structural reasons gold mining stocks consistently sell off faster and harder than the gold price itself — high operating leverage, fixed costs, equity beta, and institutional momentum — and offers a practical checklist for identifying which miners recover first when sentiment turns. The 29–49% drawdown in producers versus gold's 26% decline is framed as textbook 'beta amplification' rather than fundamental deterioration, with balance sheet strength and low-cost production identified as the two most predictive recovery traits.
